typeStatus: hypothetical — no Lexicon exists for problem records (docs/research/ATPROTO-COMMUNITY.md §7)
title: We Already Solved This
problem: Solved software problems are increasingly rediscovered from scratch instead of retrieved, and the knowledge produced while solving them rarely returns to a shared, findable place.

subproblems.statement: Existing public solutions are organised by repository, file and commit rather than by problem solved, so finding one requires knowing where it lives.

The collective judgement that made public answers usable (votes, acceptance, correction, moderation) belonged to single platforms, and problem solving is moving into private contexts where it cannot form.

hypotheses.statement: Offline, structured problem–solution records retrieve the right source for short queries more often than plain keyword search over the same sources.

A discussion can be assembled by an interface from independently owned contributions without the interface owning them: removing every relation the interface draws leaves every contribution intact and attributed.
Community signals such as endorsements, corrections and accepted fixes improve retrieval without turning it into a popularity contest.
A reader can follow any indexed answer back to its author, source and exact revision.
Agents can publish opt-in, sanitised write-ups of fixes without leaking private context.

approaches.name: Precomputed problem-oriented index
approaches.summary: Extract problem–solution records offline from pinned public sources; retrieve them at query time with cheap, deterministic, explainable ranking.

approaches.name: Portable community records
approaches.summary: Contributions live in their authors' own repositories; interfaces assemble them through declared references and clearly labelled view relations.

evidence.summary: Four Words evaluation on the labelled query set; see results for the outcome, including failures.
The Community page assembles eight fixture contributions; disconnecting all view relations leaves all eight intact. Demonstrates the boundary structurally, not federation.
Every corpus record links to its source at a pinned commit or retrieval timestamp, with licence; every site claim links to a registered source.

openQuestions: Can four words find the right answer more often than plain search over the same text, on a corpus nobody tuned?
Can one conversation be shown in independent interfaces without losing identity, order, edits or attribution?
Do endorsements, accepted fixes and tests improve relevance without becoming a popularity contest?
Is a problem a stable enough unit to index, or does it fragment into versions and contexts too quickly?
Who writes and maintains problem records, and what does that work cost?

publication.plannedCarrier: site.standard.document (exists) with this record as a payload in its open `content` union, which no reader interprets today
publication.discussion: Replies would live in their authors' own repositories and reference this record by strongRef (uri + cid), optionally a specific hypothesis id. A site.standard.document can point to a Bluesky thread through bskyPostRef; endorsement, correction and dispute records have no existing Lexicon.
